result.title: What’s harder: Asking for help or offering it? #TEDTalks #TEDIntersections
result.description: Is conversation a lost art, or is it just evolving? Journalist Joshua Johnson and social entrepreneur Blake Mycoskie answer questions on everything from the male loneliness crisis to what it actually takes to connect with others — and reveal two deceptively simple tips for going deeper with the people around you. (This conversation is part of “TED Intersections,” a series featuring thought-provoking conversations between experts navigating the ideas shaping our world.)

result.title: A New Take on an Ancient Sound | Tina Lajevardian | TED
result.description:
Musician and composer Tina Lajevardian plays a song on the oud, transforming a centuries-old Iranian musical tradition into something startlingly intimate — and proving that the oldest instruments still have new things to say. (Recorded at TED@BCG on October 23, 2025)

result.description: Have we optimized our way out of being part of communities? Introducing Corner Piece — a new podcast from TED, hosted by Answer in Progress, that asks the questions we don't usually say out loud, starting with something that so many of us are struggling with: Loneliness. result.title: How to Fix Africa’s Learning Crisis | Rapelang Rabana | TED
result.description:
By 2030, nearly half the world's young people will be African. Yet for decades, the continent's learning crisis was treated with systems unfit for reality on the ground. Social entrepreneur Rapelang Rabana shows how homegrown leadership and technology designed for African classrooms can deliver foundational skills to millions of children — and shape a new future of education across the continent. (This ambitious idea is part of The Audacious Project, TED's initiative to inspire and fund global change.) (Recorded at TED2026 on April 14, 2026)

result.title: Hip-hop gets blamed for being a bad influence — but the data shows a different story #TEDTalks
result.description: Hip-hop often gets blamed for its controversial lyrics. What if there was a way to actually measure its impact on people's lives? Analyzing 40 years' worth of radio station data and lyrics from rappers like Tupac, Dr. Dre, Jay-Z and Kendrick Lamar, economist Roland Fryer puts one of culture's most notorious debates on trial.
